title: Springy Banks Pow Wow Grounds
summary: Springy Banks at Three Mile Harbor became an intertribal gathering place for powwows in 1944 and 1945, with later gatherings continuing into the early 1950s. Montaukett, Shinnecock, Matinecock, Narragansett, Schaghticoke, Cherokee, and other Native participants met there.
address_label: Springy Banks / Three Mile Harbor, East Hampton (general)
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The Springy Banks gatherings show Native people building regional relationships during the mid-twentieth century, when public histories often spoke of Long Island's Indigenous communities only in the past. The powwows affirmed community, diplomacy, and continuing Native presence.
history_content:
Powwows were held at Springy Banks in 1944 and 1945 under the Long Island Council of the Federated Indian League. Ashby West, who used the name Red Thunder Cloud, was among the organizers. Montaukett, Shinnecock, Matinecock, Narragansett, Schaghticoke, Cherokee, and other Native people took part.

One gathering included a ceremonial "Treaty of Peace" signed by Narragansett leader Philip H. Peckham, known as Chief Night Hawk, and Montaukett leader Charles Butler, known as Chief Buckskin. Late-summer gatherings continued at Three Mile Harbor into the early 1950s and formed part of the regional powwow history in which Shinnecock participants also took part.
